comments.body:
Brainstorm + decomposition + derisk spike for alto-fruit-punch (d251) — Provision AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP; lock GitHub main to Gerrit (the code-review dogfood prerequisite).

ARC
- Re-grounded in the prior decision record (session_log slap-tripe-vat / 9dba): Gerrit-on-AWS as the un-bypassable LLM-Review merge gate, GitHub as a read-only mirror (Go topology). Independent research (GitHub-native vs GerritHub vs self-host; Gerrit project health) was run; it pressure-tested but did NOT overturn the locked decision — the rationale (kernel-vote<->label mapping, copyCondition cost lever, submitWholeTopic, exactly-one-writer topology, prior art) holds. Premise challenge dropped.
- Locked the open design questions: live PoC (priorities: function+integrity > cost > reliability/reuse-if-free); freeze-and-restore, no break-glass; AWS justified (existing acct); repo public; org free -> repo-level lockdown with trusted-admin-override accepted; domain rebar.solutions.navateam.com; infra under infra/ excluded from distribution.
- Ran a prior-art research spike (4 agents): converged reference architecture = docker-compose Gerrit (official image) + nginx (NOT Caddy, %2F) + external MCP voter on Set Review REST + core Apache replication plugin (non-force) + repo-level ruleset lockdown + cost-lean single Graviton box (no ALB/NAT, gp3, SSM Parameter Store, roll-your-own Terraform).

DECOMPOSITION (created): epic d251 now has 7 child stories S1-S7 with ACs/deps. S1 TF base; S2 Gerrit+MCP deploy+nginx/TLS; S3 project+LLM-Review label+submit-req+submitWholeTopic; S4 bot identity+events+voter (proven pipe); S5 Gerrit->GitHub replication; S6 GitHub repo lockdown; S7 e2e proof+backup/restore+monitoring+runbooks. Sequence S1<-S2<-S3<-{S4,S5}; S5<-S6; {S4,S5,S6}<-S7.

DERISK EXPERIMENTS (real AWS CLI as root of 896586841071/us-east-1 + local Docker + gh) — all green:
- E1: default VPC vpc-01fb22d3dd50a364c; AL2023 arm64 AMI via SSM param; t4g.large in all AZs; run-instances --dry-run of the exact shape OK.
- E2: PUBLIC Route53 zone solutions.navateam.com exists in-account (Z05558453EZPQLHKC20IQ) -> the subdomain is a simple A record.
- E3: SSM SecureString put/get(decrypt)/delete validated.
- E4: Gerrit 3.14.1 boots on arm64 (pin a PATCH tag — bare 3.14/3.13 don't exist); submit-req predicate label:LLM-Review=MAX AND -has:unresolved parses (HTTP 200) on live Gerrit; nginx %2F-safe proxy passes nginx -t.
- E5: navapbc/rebar public, Issues off, 0 deploy keys, I'm admin; org FREE (repo-level only); EXISTING ruleset main-protection (PR+status-checks) must be REPLACED (incompatible with mirror lock); DeployKey-bypass ruleset payload shape confirmed.

NEXT: run plan-review on the epic + each child to earn claim attestations, then S1 is the ready entry point. comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
SESSION WRAP-UP — plan-review threshold calibration + verify-budget bug + PR 86 reconciliation.

== 1. Threshold calibration (story 3d3d → PR 87, MERGED) ==
Goal: turn the advisory-by-default plan-review gate (all 32 LLM criteria at block_threshold=0.95,
posture=advisory) into calibrated per-criterion blocking defaults, from the dogfooded REVIEW_RESULT
sidecar corpus (171 sidecars / 109 tickets / 1412 findings).
Data shape: REVIEW_RESULT slim findings carry id (stable content hash), criteria[], tier (DET/LLM),
decision (block/advisory/dropped/indeterminate), validity/impact/priority (priority=validity×impact),
the 7 verifier binary sub-answers + cited_reference veto, + per-event material_fingerprint /
coverage.routing / metrics. Source-of-truth for thresholds = criteria_routing.json {block_threshold,
default_posture}; orchestrator._threshold_for maps posture→blocking_enabled, bt=min over a finding's criteria.
Signals: (A) verifier-refutation — use DENSE validity, not the sparse 'dropped' (only ~18). (B) voluntary
revision-response — material_fingerprint change between consecutive reviews = a revision; CONFOUND: exact
finding-id survival reads ~100% for LLM criteria (finder rewords each run) vs 13% for the one DET criterion,
so attribute at criterion-load-delta granularity.
Decision (Step-5 interactive): flip G6, COH, T5e, E2, G5, F1, T4 → blocking@0.70; keep FP-prone
(G1G2/T6/T5b/E5/E6/F4) and confident-but-ignored (T3/T10/T8) advisory; no policy blockers.
Sidecar enrichment (approved, UX-invisible): norm_id (reword-tolerant) + location added to sidecar
findings; test pins the surfaced library/MCP/CLI verdict is byte-unchanged.
Validation (Step 7): re-reviewed 20 high-finding/overlay tickets → 7 BLOCK / 10 PASS / 3 INDETERMINATE;
every block validity≥0.857 & impact≥0.75; 0.70 on a stable plateau (=0.75=0.80). Script+writeup in
docs/experiments/.

== 2. Verify-budget bug (bug 59bc → PR 87, MERGED) ==
The 3 INDETERMINATE in Step 7 traced to a real bug: the agentic Pass-2 verifier exhausted its 50-step
budget on finding-rich tickets; the failure was misclassified as llm_unavailable, DISCARDING the Pass-1
findings → hollow INDETERMINATE that fail-closed BLOCKS the claim. Two root causes: (1) the runner read
self._config.max_iterations, IGNORING per-request req.config (so a per-step override never reached it);
(2) the agentic verifier budget didn't scale with finding count.
Fix: runner.effective_max_iterations(floor, requested)=max(floor,requested) — a request may RAISE the
floor for one call; RunnerAgentStep scales via with:step_budget_per_item=25/finding (carried in with: since
the v3 step schema is closed); verify-step failure RECOVERED (gate_dispatch._recover_plan_review_verify_failure)
— Pass-1 findings preserved via pass3 w/ empty verifications → INDETERMINATE (no new state) + coverage.verify_failed
(≠ llm_unavailable); finalize_verdict fails OPEN unless a finding is on a blocking criterion; observability
adds usage.requests → coverage.metrics.verify_requests.
RED→GREEN: live RED (3 INDETERMINATE) → fix → live GREEN: 8e6f→BLOCK, 92fa→PASS(33 verify requests vs old
25-request ceiling), 9df3→PASS, all real verdicts. The live exercise caught a FALSE-GREEN: my budget unit
test asserted req.config (which RunnerAgentStep sets) but the live runner read self._config — the
proxy-validation anti-pattern E5 warns about; added effective_max_iterations + a consumption-path test.
PR 87 (feat/plan-review-calibration-and-verify-recovery): 2 commits, full unit suite 2465 passed,
make lint+typecheck clean (pinned ruff 0.15.19; the bare global ruff 0.15.6 false-flagged F811 on passes.py).
Also folded in a concurrent _llm_commands.py advisory-overflow CLI change (user identified the source). MERGED.

== 3. PR 86 reconciliation (task/verifier-step-telemetry) ==
PR 86 (parallel work: step-usage telemetry + completion-verifier step floor 240→480) had 6 failing pytest
jobs. Root cause: (1) test_single_turn_runner_builds_agent_with_no_tools — PR86 logged usage_limits.request_limit
but that test stubs UsageLimits as a bare object() → AttributeError; (2) PR86 predated merged PR87 and collided
(both added requests to _extract_usage + touched runner budget/telemetry). Fix: merged origin/main into the
branch (worktree tingly-wishing-nygaard); deduped requests; bound req_limit to a LOCAL used by both UsageLimits
and the telemetry logs (fixes the stub test) reporting the EFFECTIVE eff_max_iter budget; unified test requests=7.
Merge aaf70ddf6 pushed; CI GREEN (30 pass / 4 skip / 0 fail); MERGEABLE. Auto-merge left OFF (user's call).

Env note for future sessions: the pre-commit hook runs make lint/typecheck via BARE PATH tools — activate
.venv first (source .venv/bin/activate) so it uses the pinned ruff 0.15.19 + venv mypy, else it false-fails on
the global ruff 0.15.6 (F811 on passes.py) and a missing global mypy. Each worktree has its own .venv.

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
PLAN-REVIEW REMEDIATION MARATHON + FINAL STATE for d251 (alto-fruit-punch) — continued from this same log's brainstorm/decomposition/derisk/consistency-pass entries.

=== DECOMPOSITION (final) ===
Epic d251 has 9 children: S1 (TF base) 5bfc; S2 (Gerrit + review-bot RECEIVER + nginx/TLS) 786b; S3 (project/LLM-Review label/submit-req/topic) a88d; S4a (bot identity + plugins + inbound auth) 42ba; S4b (receiver review/vote logic + backfill) 918c; S5 (replication) 4e82; S6-pre (mirror-lock pre-work) dcea; S6 (apply mirror lock) 075f; S7 (e2e + backup/restore + monitoring) 3178. Clean DAG, entry points S1 + S6-pre. (If S1 is split per the pending decision -> 10 children: S1a compute/net/access + S1b DNS/secrets/backups/packaging.)

=== KEY ARCHITECTURE CORRECTIONS (from peer-pattern research + the gate) ===
- The review-bot is a thin webhook->review->vote RECEIVER that IMPORTS the review code as a library (FastAPI), NOT the stdio MCP exposed over HTTP (Gerrit posts webhooks, not MCP; FastMCP streamable-http would reject them). Stdio MCP unchanged, agent-use only.
- Gerrit webhooks plugin has NO HMAC: inbound auth = network ACL (primary) + secret-token-in-URL (necessarily lands in refs/meta/config; bounded: access-controlled, not replicated to GitHub, rotatable).
- S6 uses terraform-provider-github >=6.8.0 NATIVE DeployKey bypass (actor_type=DeployKey, bypass_mode=always, no actor_id) — dropped the entire null_resource/gh-api/two-phase/ignore_changes dance. Empirically: actor_id:null is canonical; an active deploy-key-only ruleset REJECTS an admin push (GH013).
- copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE only (dropped TRIVIAL_REBASE — it certifies a moved-base tree).
- replication: core Apache plugin, non-force, mirror=false, projects=rebar, eventsDirectory in replication.config (not gerrit.config), entrypoint hard-fails if SSM fetch fails.
- d251<->b744 SEAM = a stable adapter code_review_decision(diff)->{decision:PASS|BLOCK}. d251 'proven pipe' implements it over the EXISTING rebar.llm.review_code() (findings list -> severity-threshold decision -> LLM-Review vote, PASS->MAX, BLOCK/error->-1 fail-closed). b744-WS6 reimplements the SAME adapter over its four-pass verdict producer (gate_dispatch.produce_code_review_verdict — does NOT exist yet; b744 adds it). Receiver never calls review_code/produce_* directly, only the adapter -> drop-in swap.
- ADRs renumbered 0007-0012 (0001-0006 already taken). SSM unified under /rebar/prod/*.

=== PLAN-REVIEW GATE EXPERIENCE (dogfood signal) ===
- The gate PARSE_FAILed for ~2 sessions because ANOTHER session was mid-modifying it in this SHARED worktree (uncommitted step_budget_per_item in plan-review.yaml without the engine schema). After they landed 'calibrate per-criterion block thresholds from dogfooded data' (branch feat/plan-review-calibration-and-verify-recovery, b77e790cf), the gate works and is well-calibrated.
- PRE-calibration: non-deterministic verdicts (PASS<->BLOCK flips on unchanged/improved plans; e.g. S6 0->3->1->6 blocks), fixed ~10-advisory batch, severity-inflation (all 'critical' yet advisory), signed=True on BLOCK. I filed 2 bugs (blue-reign-quill signed-on-BLOCK; stem-poker-gecko non-determinism/calibration) then CLOSED/retracted them on instruction — that issue is owned by the other session.
- POST-calibration: convergent + every block valid. It caught real gaps in my reworking: REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM no-op on the library path; review_code returns a review_result (findings), not a verdict; produce_code_review_verdict doesn't exist yet; DLM needs a service role; refs/meta/config push must be read-modify-write; webhooks {generate:true} body; eventsDirectory location; treat_missing_data=breaching for host-crash alerting; non-force replication needs projects=. All folded in.

=== FINAL VERDICTS (gate, after remediation) ===
PASS+signed: epic, S2, S3, S4a, S5, S6, S6-pre, S7. S4b: remediated 5 rounds to implementation-depth; residual finding is an ever-deeper review_code-invocation detail (diff_text->repo_root->checkout-fetch) — captured as an ACCEPTED IMPLEMENTATION NOTE on 918c (settle vs code_review.py's real signature at build time; b744 replaces the path). S1: PASS-blocked on G5 oversize -> SPLIT decision pending with user (recommend split into S1a/S1b like S4/S6).

=== ENV / PROCESS NOTES ===
- Shared worktree with another session; now on branch feat/plan-review-calibration-and-verify-recovery (their committed gate work, 2 ahead of origin/main). Did NOT touch their files; only edited rebar tickets + editable venv reinstall.
- .venv is editable; rebuild via pip install -e .[agents]. Job tmp dir cleans s*.md between turns -> operate via rebar show/edit directly (no temp-file reliance).
- Many ticket edits left origin/tickets PUSH_PENDING (best-effort push conflicts under concurrent writes) — benign, self-heals on reconcile.

OPEN: (1) S1 split decision; (2) confirm accept S4b residual as impl-note (recommended + captured).

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
EXPERIMENT 1 — gitleaks/semgrep fit behind grounding-oracle Engine B (b744 WS5 / bba6). Tools: gitleaks 8.30.1, semgrep 1.168.0 (both installed/present), ast-grep 0.44.0. Engine B backends are EXACTLY 3 (registry.py:39-42): opengrep, ast-grep, metric; a detector = native matcher YAML rule + metadata.rebar_envelope, parsed via yaml.safe_load (registry.py:236-252); opengrep backend runs 'opengrep scan --sarif' and re-injects the envelope into rule.properties before SARIF parse (engine_b.py:297-329).
PROVEN: (a) semgrep passes arbitrary metadata (incl. a planted rebar_envelope) THROUGH VERBATIM to its JSON output extra.metadata.rebar_envelope, and emits SARIF 2.1.0 (tool 'Semgrep OSS'). opengrep is a semgrep fork sharing the YAML-rule format -> semgrep detectors drop into Engine B natively as detector YAML; this is the native path, no adapter needed.
(b) gitleaks uses TOML config (--config .toml / GITLEAKS_CONFIG_TOML) with rules COMPILED INTO the binary (no per-rule YAML file you can point --config at), so it CANNOT be expressed as an Engine B detector YAML (yaml.safe_load would reject TOML). BUT gitleaks emits SARIF 2.1.0 (schema json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0) and JSON (keys RuleID/File/StartLine/EndLine/Match/Secret/Entropy/Fingerprint). So wrapping gitleaks needs EITHER a 4th backend (BACKEND_GITLEAKS subprocess adapter) OR a generic SARIF-ingest backend that normalizes gitleaks (and any SARIF tool) -> evidence via sarif.from_sarif(trust_rebar_bag=False). The latter is the cleaner choice since semgrep ALSO emits SARIF.
(c) CRITICAL POSTURE CONFLICT: Engine B's cardinal invariant is FAIL-OPEN — a missing binary returns abstain('no_tool'), never blocks (engine_b.py:346-359; docs/grounding.md). WS5 requires FAIL-CLOSED for the secrets/High-Critical auto-block. Resolution: the fail-closed decision must live in the CONSUMER (the code-review gate / WS3 decide step) which treats abstain('no_tool'|'timeout'|'other') on a security detector as BLOCK+coverage-gap — NOT inside the oracle. (d) lint.py:33-79 'gitleaks-style' scan is an in-house 8-pattern regex, NOT the gitleaks binary.

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
EXPERIMENT 2 — Gerrit webhook->diff gap (d251 S4a/S4b). Ran a REAL read-only experiment against the live public Gerrit gerrit-review.googlesource.com (no docker needed). PROVEN:
(a) Change-metadata JSON (GET /changes/?q=...&o=CURRENT_REVISION) is XSSI-guarded with the )]}' prefix and carries NO diff/patch field (HAS_DIFF_FIELD: False) — the webhooks-plugin payload is an EVENT (patchset-created metadata), strictly less than this, so the diff is NEVER in the webhook body.
(b) GET /changes/{n}/revisions/current/patch returns a BASE64 blob (first chars 'RnJvbSBi...'), which base64-decodes to a git format-patch ('From <sha> Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 / Subject: [PATCH] ...'). So the receiver MUST make a separate authenticated REST call to obtain the diff; it must base64-decode the result.
(c) GET /changes/{n}/revisions/current/files/ returns JSON (XSSI-guarded) — the structured per-file alternative.
IMPLICATION: d251 S4b (918c) already has Round-9 AC ('fetches diff via Gerrit REST as diff_text=') and Round-10 AC ('invokes review_code() with a valid repo context / fetched checkout at the change ref'). The GAP the review caught is that the EPIC body's Round-9 seam still types the adapter as code_review_decision(diff_text)->{decision} (diff_text ONLY), contradicting S4b's Round-10 reality (needs diff_text + repo_root + ref). REMEDY: reconcile the epic seam contract to code_review_decision(diff_text, repo_root, ref)->{decision: PASS|BLOCK}, give it a concrete name+module, co-locate the error/fallback rule with the schema, and add an explicit covering AC; b744-WS6 (4119) must implement the SAME signature. Also: provision the bot's OUTBOUND read credential (Gerrit HTTP token works for REST /a/ AND git-over-HTTPS clone of the change ref) in S1 SSM scaffolding + S4a.

EXPERIMENT 3 — discriminates_novelty bar (7d43 BLOCK). The eval scorers (eval_scorers.py:212-257) are PER-CASE booleans at a 0.5 midpoint: _discriminates_true_from_false uses v>=0.5; _discriminates_impact_levels uses imp>=_IMPACT_MAJOR_FLOOR(0.5). The spec (plan-review-verifier.eval.yaml) gates at the SPEC level: gate: at_least(2) over epochs:3 + coverage_threshold:0.8; deterministic discriminators carry NO per-scorer threshold field (only the llm-judge scorer has threshold:0.7, gates:false). So THREE distinct numbers were being conflated: (1) RUNTIME drop threshold T_novel=0.7 (Pass-3: novelty<0.7 => treat as carryover/floored) — house precision-first default, config-overridable; (2) the eval per-case discrimination floor = 0.5 midpoint (mirror the two sibling discriminators); (3) the eval BAR = spec gate at_least(2)/epochs:3 + coverage_threshold:0.8 over a labeled novel/carryover pair set. The BLOCK is about #3 (and its relationship to #2). RESOLUTION recorded into 7d43 + child 150b.

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body: REMEDIATION APPLIED (Round-11, 2026-06-29). 7d43: BLOCK fixed (discriminates_novelty bar = per-case 0.5 midpoint + spec gate at_least(2)/epochs:3/coverage 0.8, distinct from runtime T_novel=0.7); child title/body swaps fixed (ec89↔3689 restored to match titles, 3689 de-duplicated vs 4cb9); ownership pinned (cc5b owns T_novel+floor+sidecar-write+evidence-gate; ec89 owns freshness-window+code-change-detection via verified_at_sha; default-on→default-OFF expand-contract); novelty sub-answer arithmetic + fail-safe defined on 150b+epic. b744: WS5/bba6 rewritten with experiment-grounded detector design (semgrep native opengrep YAML; gitleaks via generic SARIF-ingest backend; fail-closed in the consumer not the oracle); WS1/WS2/WS3/WS4/WS6 got targeted ACs (recommend_overlays schema+base-failure fallback; threshold-resolver handoff; merge_findings dedup+overlay_union already-run input+escalation ADR+gate-yaml schema; disabled-shim return + one-way-door correction + stale-refs; staged rollout + coverage-gap vote UX); epic reconciled + disposition comment. d251: epic Round-11 section reconciles the adapter seam to code_review_decision(diff_text,repo_root,ref) [fixes the Round-9/Round-10 contradiction], webhook-no-diff base64 REST fetch (PROVEN), outbound read credential, SSM scaffolding (alert-endpoint+bot-token), EC2-role/gerrit.config/DLM ownership contracts, BSL citation; S1/S4a/S4b/S5 child ACs added; disposition comment (incl. already-addressed items justified).
